ROOT_CAUSE: Two independent defects in the current episode write path, with a third audit finding that is not a defect at all. (1) The runtime gated capture_backend on execution.executed, but that field's own docstring defines it as 'the channel that produced THIS episode's before/after frames'. Those are different questions, so a failed action that still had a real frame on disk reported capture_backend="" -- and because empty was already documented to mean 'no action reached a backend', two meanings collapsed into one value and a reader could interpret neither. (2) executor.py built the PRESS_BACK result without a recognition_backend argument, so it defaulted to ""; the executor router explicitly reports "NONE" for that same action. The same action therefore recorded different provenance depending on which path ran it. (3) The third gap is NOT a defect: the runtime returns at runtime.py before _record_episode for SAFE_STOP, so an all-empty row can never be produced by the runtime.
CHANGED_FILES: winter_agent_v2/runtime.py (capture_backend now gated on the frames existing rather than on the action having executed)
winter_agent_v2/executor.py (PRESS_BACK declares recognition_backend="NONE", matching what the router already reported)

REMAINING_ISSUE: Three honest limits. (1) The two fixed paths are proven at unit and REPLAY level, not live: the 15:16:47Z row had executed=true, so it does not by itself exercise the executed=false path that cause 1 was about, and no ADB-dispatched BACK was recorded live this session (the 13:35:26Z BACK ran on MAA and already reported NONE). Natural production traffic is what will exercise them; the next audit should confirm no new rows appear with those shapes rather than assume it. (2) The single SAFE_STOP row with all four fields empty cannot come from the runtime, so some other writer appends to learning/episodes.jsonl. That writer was not identified; the finding is pinned by a test so it cannot be lost, but anyone computing failure rates from this stream should know the stream is not exclusively runtime-produced. (3) The audit's 'completeness' counts non-empty fields; it does not verify that each value is TRUE. Nothing here checks that a row claiming MAA actually ran MAA. That was outside this work order's scope and remains open.
